purpose: turn a business problem into analyzed needs, process models and options with costs and benefits, so the right thing gets specified
entry_criteria: A business problem or opportunity is stated
procedure: Describe the current process end to end (who, steps, systems, volumes, delays and error rates) using observation and data, not only descriptions.
Model it with a standard notation such as BPMN, and mark where work waits, loops back or is done by hand.
Find root causes with a method such as five whys or cause-and-effect analysis, and test each cause against data.
Define options including the do-nothing case, and compare them on cost, benefit, risk and effort with the assumptions shown.
Recommend an option and state the measurable change expected, such as handling time or error rate, with the baseline.
Hand over the analysis and the recommendation to requirements work with the open questions listed.
deliverables: recommendation with baseline and expected change
acceptance_criteria: Process models match what people do, confirmed by them
Do-nothing is one of the options
The expected benefit has a baseline

validation.check: walk two process participants through the model and record corrections
recompute the benefit estimate from the cited baseline figures

failure_modes.mode: Model shows the official process, not the real one

failure_modes.response: Add do-nothing and a cheaper option

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: Observation shows invoice approvals wait a median of 6 days, mostly for one approver. Options are compared, including a delegation rule, and the recommendation targets a 2-day median with the 6-day figure as the baseline.
